text:
alyssa: quick sanity-check — i'm drafting the fallback compatibility checklist for smart routing by tier+region. goal: safe fallback from full LLM -> quantized-small when quota or capacity hits. need tokenizer/context/tool parity checks.

mike: low-level: biggest risk is broken tool-calls (args order, JSON schema) and truncated prompts when context differs.

raj: agree. also watch for kv-cache layout changes in some quantized builds — it can shift token indexing by 1 for certain bpe variants.

alyssa: ugh. concrete ask: can we define a small acceptance matrix we can gate in the console rollout UI? thinking columns: model-variant, tokenizer-match (yes/partial/no), max-context, toolcall-parity (schema_ok|needs_adapter), known-truncation-risks, telemetry-flag.

sarah: love that. example row: `gptx-32k -> gptx-q8-32k` tokenizer-match=yes, max-context=32768, toolcall-parity=schema_ok, truncation-risk=low, telemetry-flag=fallback_reason.

mike: but for `gptx-32k -> gptx-q4-16k` tokenizer-match=partial, max-context=16384, toolcall-parity=needs_adapter (kwargs reorder), truncation-risk=medium. need a tiny adapter layer in router to rewrite toolcall payloads.

alyssa: can we avoid adapters for 1.0? ops wants minimal surface area. if adapter needed, mark as blocked for auto-fallback and require manual canary.

raj: that's reasonable. we should also emit a `fallback_compat_level` metric: values {green,yellow,red} per request so telemetry can backfill compatibility across customers.

ops-bot: deploy check passed for router-v3 on staging at 2026-05-12T09:40:12Z :white_check_mark:

jess: small UX note: on the rollout console, show a single toggle "enable auto-fallback" + a "compatibility preview" that lists affected routes and a warning if any route has red compatibility. can we compute preview server-side?

mike: yes, server-side simulation possible: run the request through a lightweight compatibility checker using sample prompts from the route. cost: tiny, but we can cache results per route+model-variant.

alyssa: okay let's draft the compatibility checker algorithm in this thread. rough: 1) run sample prompts through tokenizer of primary and candidate variant. 2) compare tokenization sequences; if mismatch ratio > 2% -> partial. 3) simulate tool-call: apply model-specific tool schemas and validate produced tool-call JSON shape (we have model tool-call shim for each variant). 4) check max-context by encoding prompt + expected completion length.

mike: pseudo: ```python
def compat_check(samples, primary, candidate):
    t1 = tokenize(primary, samples)
    t2 = tokenize(candidate, samples)
    token_mismatch = mean([levenshtein(t1[i], t2[i]) / len(t1[i]) for i in range(len(samples))])
    tool_ok = all(validate_tool(schema_for(primary), schema_for(candidate), s) for s in samples)
    context_ok = max(encoded_len(samples)+expected_completion) <= candidate.max_context
    return {"token_mismatch": token_mismatch, "tool_ok": tool_ok, "context_ok": context_ok}
```

raj: two operational points: (a) sample set must be tenant-specific (some customers use long system prompts), (b) telemetry must tag which sample triggered mismatch for regression triage.

alyssa: yes on both. add event `compat_preview.sample_id` in telemetry and store hashed sample id to avoid PII.

sarah: question on rollout policy: if compatibility is yellow (partial), do we auto-fallback for low-tier customers only or not at all? ops thinks fallback for low-tier is ok but enterprise disabled by default.

ops-bot: note: enterprise plan contracts require manual approval for model variant changes per account (ticket automation available).

mike: implement policy matrix: if tenant.tier == "enterprise" && compat_level != green -> block auto-fallback. else if tenant.tier == "standard" and region in high-latency -> allow fallback if compat_level != red. low-tier -> allow fallback unless red.

jess: add console affordance: per-tenant override with audit trail + reason field (free text limited to 200 chars).

raj: telemetry fields we should emit on fallback event: `fallback_from`, `fallback_to`, `compat_level`, `token_mismatch_pct`, `toolcall_errors` (count), `trigger` (quota|latency|manual), `sample_hash`.

alyssa: also emit `router_decision_v` so we can evolve heuristics.

mike: edge-case: tool-calling parity could be syntactic but semantically different — we can't fully verify. add a regression alert that compares historical tool-call success rates pre/post fallback. if success dips > 3% -> rollback.

raj: agree. set a temporary canary window: 1 hour with 1% of traffic for auto-fallback when compat_level==green, require manual canary for yellow.

sarah: can we include a per-route dry-run toggle where router logs what it would have done without actually failing over? helpful for safety.

mike: yes. router already supports `--dry-run` mode. will expose via API: `route.update({"auto_fallback": true, "dry_run_preview": true})`.

alyssa: last: who's owning the compatibility table? ops + eng-runtime pair? i'll take coordination but need owners for tokenizer tests (mike) and tool-call shim cert (raj).

mike: i'll add tokenizer test harness to explainer project.

raj: i'll own tool-call shim cert + telemetry events.

jess: i'll draft console mockups for the preview + per-tenant override. will post images in #design next.

alyssa: thanks. next steps: mike/raj implement checks, produce spec PR, jess sends mockups, i'll wire gating in rollout API. aim for staging canary next week. :raised_hands:

ops-bot: reminder: create a cross-team RFC for this and tag `#security` for review (automated rule).

mike: noted. will open PR today.

sarah: +1 on RFC. if we keep metrics and canary windows strict, i'm good.

alyssa: cool. closing loop here. if anyone finds an existing variant with mismatched tokenizer, drop sample in thread and tag me.
